items.description: An earlier commit dropped `searchText` from the contributor search query, so the MultiSelect only ever fetched one fixed page of 50 client users and filtered client-side with no server search. Any client user outside that first page of 50 became invisible and unaddable, a functional regression from the prior combobox which server-searched all clients.

items.acceptance_evidence: Accepted on the review thread (identifiers redacted).
items.description: Once the sidebar gate was removed, beneficiaries could reach the manage-team panel and see the contributor slot as editable, but the underlying candidate query hits `GET /api/users/list`, which is admin-only and 403s for client sessions. A beneficiary could remove a contributor but never add one, contradicting the panel's own subtitle claiming they could do both.

items.acceptance_evidence: Accepted on the review thread (identifiers redacted).
items.description: This PR removed the `!isBeneficiary` gate (added five days earlier in #2650) around the team section, so all client users could suddenly see 1st/2nd chair attorney, paralegal, and hiring-manager assignments with no feature flag protecting the change, despite `feature-flags.mdc` requiring one for removing an existing UI flow.

Every implicit bulk-deselect surface of the MultiSelect could revoke collaborator access with no confirmation: the trigger's clear-all fired `onValueChange([])` removing everyone in one click, and the "+N more" badge's clear button truncated to the default `maxCount` of 3, silently dropping every collaborator past the first three chips.

items.acceptance_evidence: Not accepted; author declined on the review thread (identifiers redacted).
items.description: A multi-add or clear-all fires N parallel mutations, and each response writes its own full-team snapshot via `setQueryData` right after only its own request completed. If an earlier snapshot lands last, it can resurrect already-removed members in the cache, and the MultiSelect's chips sync straight from that cache.

items.acceptance_evidence: Accepted on the review thread (identifiers redacted).
items.description: The `cw:case-updated` realtime publish never refreshed the team panel for other open sessions: the listener invalidated the tasks/details/snapshot query keys but not the team key, and `refetchOnWindowFocus` was off, so collaborator changes appeared stale until a manual remount.

items.description: Key paths of `removeCaseContributor` were unpinned by tests: no test rejects removal on an archived case, the realtime publish is stubbed but never asserted, there is no publish-throws test (unlike sibling flows), and the idempotent no-op test checks only that `removeMember` wasn't called rather than the no-event invariant its sibling pins.

items.description: The hook mocks in this test file take no arguments, so the component's `onSuccess`/`onError` mutation options never run in any test — meaning the new error-recovery behavior (`multiSelectRef.current?.reset()` restoring a chip after a failed remove), toasts, and cache writes are all uncovered.

items.description: The contributor domain events mix vocabularies in what is meant to be an append-only stream: assignment keeps the old single-slot shape with a now-permanently-null `previousContributorId`, while removal introduces a new set-based shape, and lawyer/paralegal removal is still modeled as an assignment with `new: null`.

items.description: Adding and removing a collaborator are new primary user actions but ship with no analytics events, even though the adjacent team section already tracks a panel-opened event and the facade service already injects `AnalyticsService` without using it here.

items.description: If the domain-event publish throws after `removeMember` has already committed, the removal stands permanently with no corresponding `domain_event` row, and a retry hits the method's early `!isContributor` return so the event can never be recovered — unlike the sibling lawyer-assignment flow, which has a synthetic backfill this flow doesn't.

items.description: While a mutation is pending, `disabled` only reaches the MultiSelect's trigger button — the open popover stays interactive, items keep a pointer cursor, and clicks silently no-op — so rapid multi-adds during an in-flight request lose selections with no visible feedback to the user.

items.acceptance_evidence: Not accepted; author declined on the review thread (identifiers redacted). Commits referenced: ca0c2643cb0d, d561728b78c9, 932bc9dcf.
items.description: The guard only checks that the target holds a `contributor` row, but the removal call (`removeMember` → `unsyncCaseRoleAssignments`) deletes every case role and FGA tuple the target holds with no role filter, and users can hold multiple case roles. A beneficiary authorized only to manage the contributor slot could therefore also silently revoke a target's staff-role grants, with only `removedContributorId` recorded in the event.
`multiSelectRef` was declared after the two `onError` closures that reference it, which only worked because those closures run post-mount rather than at declaration time.

items.description: The add-contributor path opened with a plain `findOne`, so an archived case returned a generic "Case not found" 404 on add but a "Case is archived" 409 on remove — two different error shapes for the same underlying constraint on one control.
